main_text.p: Est igitur hæc postrema oratio [illegible, ~9 letters].

Status,2. Status iuredicialis est.Hoc enim quæritur,Iurène,an uerò iniuria Ionæ doleat, quòd cucurbita interijsset,quæ umbracu li uice (sancto prophetæ,Dei nomine in tantas angustias coniecto,ut mors etiam ei expetenda uideretur) fuerat: & quòd Niniuitis,quibus internecionem denun- ciari Dominus uoluerat,parceret?Negan tem sententiam Deus tuetur: aientem ue rò Ionas propheta.Occurrit autem,ut uidetis,hoc loco exemplum hominis alio- quin sancti & prudentis,qui tamen in te- tationis [illegible, ~12 letters] modestiæ nonihil ob- litus,Deo ex aduerso respondit. Vtinam uerò,infirmitatis & gradus nostri confci- entia, & summi istius uiri offensa com- monefacti,nunquam non Dei,cuius ma- gna & mirabilia opera sunt, iudicia ado- remus,ut maximè causæ & destinata nos longo tempore fugiant. Satis enim hoc nobis esse debet, quòd Deû omnia quæ uult,in cœlo & in terra facere scimus: Psal.115.3. Nam eius uoluntas iustissima, optima & sapientissima est.
Syllogismus principalis.3. Argumetum quo Deus utitur ad co-vincendum Ionam, ducitur ab ἀντιθέσει

page.notes: Greek word in the first line (ending the continued paragraph) is not legible; marked as illegible. The Greek word after "tationis" is not legible at this scan resolution; marked as illegible. The Greek word after "ducitur ab" is printed as ἀντιθέσει, read with some doubt. The number in "Psal.115.3." is read as 115 and may be damaged. The running head "PRAELECTIONES" and page number 392 are as printed. The final "præiu-" is the catchword: a word broken at the foot, printed below the last line.
